newsitem.title: THAILAND: Canada team wraps up Asia trip with Thai deals.
newsitem.headline: Canada team wraps up Asia trip with Thai deals.

text.p: A Canadian government and business delegation accompanying Prime Minister Jean Chretien on a four-day visit to Thailand signed 55 deals worth over C$1.0 billion ($746.3 million) on Friday.
"We are finishing our third visit to the Pacific with a big bang," Chretien said at a ceremony to sign the deals.
Thailand is the final stop on a three-nation Asian tour for Chretien and his 400-strong "Team Canada" trade delegation.
The Thai business brought the total to 180 new deals signed during the Asian mission worth C$2.13 billion, a Canadian official said.

The business deals signed in Thailand included C$614.09 million in commercial contracts and $407.74 million in agreements in principle, including memoranda of understanding and letters of intent, the statement said.
"This is the icing on the cake," a government official said of the Thai deals. Team Canada signed 73 deals worth C$602.57 million in South Korea and 52 deals worth C$505.58 in the Philippines.
Chretien credited Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh for helping resolve last minute problems with some of the deals.
"Mr Prime Minister, because of you...you made a quick decision. We love it. We have managed to go over C$1.0 billion. And it's the beginning," Chretien said.

One of the major deals announced on Friday, a C$155 million contract for Canada's Spar Aerospace Ltd to construct a remote sensing satellite system, survived only because of intervention by both the Thai and Canadian leaders, government and business sources said.

"Both prime ministers played a very important role, and certainly the visit of the Canadian prime minister was critical to resolve this kind of issue at a very high level," Karsten Westphal, Spar's vice-president international, told reporters.
He would not give details, saying only the premiers helped resolve the payment schedule for the contract.
Thailand has said it will cut all unnecessary spending in the next few fiscal years in an effort to trim its growing current account deficit and help boost the sagging economy.
The satellite deal was reportedly one of the projects that could have been shelved.
Chretien told a business lunch earlier in the day the visit to Bangkok was a way of showing that Canada hoped to move its relationship with Thailand to a new level.

"Our decision to make Bangkok a key stop on our mission is testimony to our commitment to a new economic partnership with Thailand," he said. "We also want to demonstrate to Thai business people that Canada is an ideal partner for the challenges facing Thaiand today."

Major deals signed between the two countries range from a five-year one million tonne wheat sale to Thai flour mills to the Spar contract to a C$200 million telecommunciations contract for Northern Telecom Ltd
Chretien said the goal for the two countries was to have C$2.0 billion in trade by 2000. Two-way trade in 1995 amounted to C$1.6 billion.
